categories.main_business_segments: DXC operates through two primary business segments: Global Business Services (GBS) and Global Infrastructure Services (GIS). GBS focuses on consulting, engineering, applications, and insurance software and business process services, while GIS provides cloud, IT outsourcing, security, and modern workplace solutions. Both segments serve a broad range of industries and are designed to help clients modernize and optimize their IT environments.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: DXC leverages advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI), data analytics, cloud computing (public, private, and hybrid), mainframe modernization, and automation. The company employs a mix of proprietary software, custom engineering, and integration of third-party solutions, with a strong emphasis on secure-by-design methodologies and AI-driven intelligent operations. Service delivery is supported by a global workforce and a virtual-first operating model.
categories.primary_customers_markets: DXC serves a global client base that includes many Fortune 500 companies, commercial enterprises of all sizes, and public sector organizations. Key industries include finance, insurance, automotive, manufacturing, healthcare, life sciences, travel, and government. The company’s offerings are tailored to address industry-specific challenges and digital transformation objectives.
categories.geographic_coverage: DXC operates in over 60 countries, with significant revenue generated from the United States, United Kingdom, other European countries, Australia, and other international markets. Approximately 72% of fiscal 2025 revenues were derived from outside the U.S., reflecting a broad international presence and diverse customer base.
categories.supply_chain_position: DXC is positioned as a downstream IT services provider, delivering end-to-end solutions directly to enterprise and public sector clients. The company integrates and manages technology infrastructure, applications, and business processes, often acting as a systems integrator and managed services partner rather than a supplier of raw materials or hardware.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: DXC’s strategic priorities center on customer-centric innovation, cost optimization, and market expansion. The company is investing in AI, cloud migration, cybersecurity, and digital transformation services, with a focus on integrating generative AI into offerings and enhancing automation. R&D efforts are directed at developing differentiated, scalable solutions that address emerging technology trends and evolving client needs.
categories.revenue_model: DXC generates revenue primarily through long-term service contracts, including time and materials, unit-price, and fixed-price agreements, as well as software licensing and business process outsourcing. Revenue streams include IT outsourcing, consulting, engineering, cloud and security services, and proprietary insurance software solutions, with recurring revenues from managed services and support.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: DXC competes in a highly competitive global IT services market against large multinational firms (such as Accenture, IBM, and Tata Consultancy Services), specialized niche providers, offshore service companies (notably in India), and in-house IT departments. The company differentiates itself through integrated solutions, industry expertise, global delivery capabilities, and a focus on modernization and security.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For fiscal year 2025, DXC reported revenues of $12.87 billion, a 5.8% decline from the prior year, with adjusted EBIT of $1.02 billion and net income of $396 million. The company has a global workforce of over 120,000 employees and maintains investment-grade credit ratings, though it is experiencing revenue contraction as it transitions its business model and optimizes its portfolio.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: DXC emphasizes its ability to help clients modernize mission-critical systems, integrate AI-powered intelligence, and ensure security and compliance across complex IT estates. The company’s value proposition is built on deep industry expertise, global scale, secure-by-design solutions, and the ability to deliver measurable business outcomes through innovative, tailored technology services.
